title: create is about 3% slower after the LCP unification, from code layout
body:
After the LCP unification (sufr-caa3f2, commit noted in its close reason), `sufr -t 4 create --dna --write-lcp` on a 50 MB synthetic DNA input takes 2.440 s against 2.361 s before (+3.3%), and `create --dna -m 20` takes 2.615 s against 2.552 s (+2.5%). Medians of 5 interleaved release runs. `locate` is 9% faster and `locate -l` 2% faster.

The new build executes 6% fewer instructions (126.4G against 134.8G) but 2-4% more cycles. Placing the previous builder and util code unchanged into the new tree gives a byte-identical `merge_sort` and the same instruction count, and still costs +4% cycles. Adding the new lcp.rs functions to the old tree unused costs nothing. So the slowdown follows from where the code sits in the binary, not from the routine. Forcing 64-byte loop alignment did not recover it.

The scripts, input generator and timings are in `tmp-claude/2026-11-02-refactor-survey/step4/`.

## Open

Whether to chase the layout with PGO or BOLT, or accept the cost.
